items.definition: Confident, fluent output that is simply wrong, especially a fact, a citation or a number that does not exist.
items.example: It invented a reference that looks perfect and does not exist.

items.definition: The instruction and the context you give a model. Writing a good one is a real skill, not a magic formula.
items.example: A one-line prompt gave me a generic answer; a prompt with the audience and the length gave me a usable one.

items.definition: A fraudulent message, usually by email, designed to steal credentials or money by pretending to be someone you trust.
items.example: That email about a locked account was phishing, and it used our bank's real logo.

items.definition: Phishing carried out by text message. Short, urgent, and arriving on the phone you are holding.
items.example: The message about a parcel was smishing, and the link was not the courier's website.

items.definition: Phishing carried out by a phone call, usually with a claim of authority from a bank, a police force or a support line.
items.example: They called pretending to be the tax office. That is vishing, and I hung up and called the real number.

items.definition: Presenting a false sender identity so that a call or a message appears to come from a number or address that belongs to someone else.
items.example: The message showed my brother's name, but the number was spoofed.

items.definition: The short number a bank sends to confirm a login or a payment. Anyone who holds it can complete the action.
items.example: I gave them the one-time code, and that was the moment the account was theirs.

items.definition: A bank account used to receive and pass on criminal money, sometimes opened by someone who believes they are helping a company or a cause.
items.example: They asked me to receive money and pass it on. That makes my account a mule account and the money is stolen.

items.definition: A reversal of a card payment requested from the bank, usually because the transaction was not authorised or the goods never arrived.
items.example: The bank raised a chargeback and returned the money five days later.

items.definition: Money demanded before a service is delivered. Common in fake job offers, fake investments and fake love interests.
items.example: They wanted a small fee before the equipment arrived, and then a larger one.

items.definition: The chunk of text a model reads or writes. Usually a word, a part of a word, or a common symbol.
items.example: The word "the" is one token, and a long word may be three.

items.definition: The fixed vocabulary a model uses, plus the rule that splits text into tokens and joins them back.
items.example: A different tokenizer means the same text costs a different number of tokens.

items.definition: The maximum number of tokens a model can hold at once, counting the question, the history, the documents and the instructions together.
items.example: With an 8,000 token window, a 9,000 token request has to be cut.

items.definition: The tokens you send, counted and billed on the way in. Documents and chat history both count here.
items.example: Uploading the same file twice charges the input tokens twice.

items.definition: The tokens the model generates, counted and billed on the way out. Long answers cost more than short ones.
items.example: Asking for 2,000 words doubles the output cost of asking for 200.

items.definition: The setting that controls how random the choice of the next token is. Lower values are more repeatable, higher values more varied and less reliable.
items.example: For extracting data from a document, keep the temperature low.

items.definition: The automatic cutting of input that is longer than the context window, usually removing the oldest part.
items.example: Truncation is why the model never mentions the first page you uploaded.

items.definition: The card or phone screen that lets you board the aircraft. It carries your name, the flight, the gate, the seat and the boarding time.
items.example: Show your boarding pass at the gate and find your seat.

items.definition: The secure part of the airport where you wait for a connecting flight. You cannot leave it without a new ticket.
items.example: My flight is delayed, so I am stuck in the transit area.

items.definition: The door onto the aircraft, identified by a letter and a number, for example B22. It is assigned late and can change.
items.example: My gate has changed from B22 to C4.

items.definition: The area where the belt for your flight delivers your suitcase. The belt number is shown on the screens above it.
items.example: Your bag is on belt 7, and it has been there for ten minutes.

items.definition: A connection between two flights at the same airport, without going through the city in between.
items.example: I have a two-hour transfer in Singapore.

items.definition: The checkpoint where bags and people are checked before entering the secure part of the airport.
items.example: Security screening starts at the end of this corridor.

items.definition: The rule limiting containers of liquid in hand baggage, usually to 100 ml each in a clear bag.
items.example: My bottle is 500 ml, so I have to empty it before screening.

items.definition: The border desk where an officer checks your passport and your right to enter or leave the country.
items.example: Passport control is straight ahead, and baggage claim is on the left.

items.definition: The place where you declare goods over the allowance. Most travellers use the green or white channel for nothing to declare.
items.example: Do I go through the red channel if I bought two bottles of wine?

items.definition: The moment you take the room, normally from 14:00 or 15:00. Before it, the hotel usually stores your luggage free of charge.
items.example: Check-in is from 14:00, but I can leave my bags with you in the morning.

items.definition: The card or fob that opens your door. In many hotels it also works as your room number, your lift pass and your breakfast voucher.
items.example: Could I have a second key card for my colleague?

items.definition: A sum held on your card, or taken in cash, to cover extras and damage. It is released after you leave.
items.example: We hold a deposit of 200 on your card for the minibar and the safe.

items.definition: Giving the room back and paying the final bill, usually between 10:00 and 12:00. Late check-out can often be arranged.
items.example: Can I check out at 14:00 instead of 11:00? My flight is at 17:00.

items.definition: Free storage of bags before check-in or after check-out, which lets you use the city without carrying a suitcase.
items.example: Could you store my luggage until my flight in the evening?

items.definition: The team that cleans the rooms, changes the linen and takes away used towels.
items.example: Could housekeeping bring two more towels, please?

items.definition: The staff member who arranges tickets, tours, taxis, doctors and anything else the hotel does not sell itself.
items.example: The concierge booked a table at a restaurant that was fully booked.

items.definition: The list of dishes a kitchen offers, with prices and short descriptions.
items.example: Could we see the menu, please?

items.definition: A starter, a main course and a dessert sold together at a single price. Often the cheapest and most predictable choice.
items.example: I will take the set menu, please.

items.definition: The small first course, such as soup, a salad or fried snacks.
items.example: As a starter, I will have the soup.

items.definition: The main dish of the meal, usually the largest and most expensive item.
items.example: What would you recommend for the main course?

items.definition: The sweet course at the end of the meal, or the sweet things served with coffee.
items.example: Do you have any sugar-free desserts?

items.definition: A rule you follow about what you eat, often religious or ethical, such as halal, kosher, vegetarian or vegan.
items.example: Do you have any halal dishes that do not contain pork?

items.definition: The list of what you ordered and what you owe. In America it is called the check.
items.example: Could we have the bill, please? Is service included?
